Although the plasmonic metal is crucial, surface-bound molecules actively participate by scavenging charge carriers, affecting selectivity and stability, and even undergoing chemical transformations. These aspects are crucial for controlling product distributions and enabling novel chemical pathways by exploiting excited-state pathways inaccessible through thermal energy. Together with the nanoscale properties of plasmonic nanostructures, chemical reactions can be confined to nanoscale hot spots shaped by geometry and polarization. These insights inform the development of practical design principles for antenna–reactor hybrids and novel plasmonic materials in which absorption, carrier localization, and interfacial alignment are precisely engineered. Finally, we identify key open questions and the need for operando interfacial techniques to transform these insights into practical tools for selective, solar-driven synthesis.
items.authors: Sergio Kogikoski Junior, Wouter Koopman, Felix Stete, Radwan M. Sarhan, Shashank K.Gahlaut, Evgenii Titov
items.title_zh: 分子-金属纳米结构在等离子体化学中的相互作用
items.summary_zh: 等离子体化学通过分子-金属界面的三个相互关联的通道将金属纳米结构转化为光催化剂：增强的近场、非平衡电荷载体和局部热量。本文重点讨论这一界面视角，展示了吸附物和配体不仅仅是附着在纳米颗粒上，它们还会降低等离子体寿命、改变功函数、修改态密度，并影响各种物理过程中的能量和电荷流动。在脉冲激发下的超快热化和连续照明下的稳态条件下，为化学反应开辟了不同的途径。尽管等离子体金属至关重要，但表面结合的分子通过捕获电荷载体积极参与，影响选择性和稳定性，甚至经历化学转化。这些方面对于控制产物分布和利用激发态途径实现新型化学反应至关重要。结合等离子体纳米结构的纳米尺度特性，化学反应可以被限制在由几何形状和极化所塑造的纳米级热点中。这些见解为天线-反应器混合体和新型等离子体材料的实用设计原则的发展提供了指导。

items.title: Modulation of Crystal Habit and Preferred Orientation of Aspirin: Combined Effects of Solvent and a Metallic Mesh Template during Evaporative Crystallization
items.abstract: Polymorphism plays a significant role in crystal engineering, as it can directly influence the physicochemical properties of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Aspirin (ASA) is one of the extensively studied model compounds in small-molecule polymorphism due to its pharmaceutical relevance. To date, ASA has been reported to exist in four polymorphic forms, Forms I, II, III, and IV. Like polymorphism, preferred (or preferential) orientation is another important characteristic in solidform screening that increases the risk of misidentifying pharmaceutical compounds as polymorphs. Here, we report evaporative crystallization of Form I ASA, with and without a metallic mesh template, in solvents of different polarities, exhibiting preferred orientation driven by the resulting crystal morphology 2 while retaining Form I. It was observed that the solvent and/or template independently/combinedly, along with grinding, has induced the preferred orientation of Form I ASA modulated by crystal habit during some crystallization conditions. Consequently, this study may provide a rationale for preventing the misidentification of crystal polymorphs during pharmaceutical manufacturing and development.
items.authors: Kelina Cyril Anthoni, Divya S. Sujith, Indumathi Sathisaran

items.title: Not comparing like with like: a measurement-conditions audit of the solid polymer electrolyte literature
items.abstract: Ionic conductivities of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are routinely compared across publications as though they were measured the same way. We tested that assumption by building a measurement-conditions annotation layer over the largest open compilation of SPE conductivity data (16,009 measurements from 214 source papers), recording for each source study how the measurement was actually made. Fifty-eight papers spanning 1986–2020 and 20 journals were annotated across 59 fields, covering 11,394 measurements, or 71.2% of the compilation. Every condition was extracted twice independently and all substantive disagreements were adjudicated against the source PDFs. Three findings follow. First, 22.5% of the compilation’s measurements come from systems containing no polymer at all—salts in molecular solvents or ionic liquids, classified from the declared composition alone. These sit a median 2.6 orders of magnitude above solvent-free SPEs while being measured 35 řC cooler, and they inflate any pooled statistic drawn from the dataset. Second, refitting each formulation’s temperature series and extrapolating to 25 řC shows that among genuinely solvent-free polymer electrolytes, 50.1% reach 10−4 S cm−1 at the temperature reported but only 3.4% do so at 25 řC, a median loss of 2.54 orders; 97.5% of their best-reported values are taken at ≥60 řC. Pooling classes understates this attrition because liquid systems barely lose anything on cooling. Third, the conditions needed to reproduce or even recompute a conductivity are frequently absent: film thickness is not recoverable for 60.7% of papers, electrode area for 68.4%, per-point equilibration time for 77.2%, and only 5 of 57 papers report a measured residual water content.
items.authors: Om Chaudhari

items.title: Atomic Orbital Interactions in [CeX6]2– (X = F, Cl, Br): Consequences for X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopic Analysis
items.abstract: Metal–ligand bonding in [CeX 6 ] 2– complexes (X = F, Cl, Br) is investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and pre-bonding analysis. The analysis quantifies atomic orbital (AO) energies and overlaps in the complexes, with a focus on the mixing between Ce 4f AOs with halide 𝑛p donor AOs. Results indicate that decreasing Ce–ligand AO overlap from X = F to Br is compensated by improved AO energy matching, leading to increased 4f-based ligand-to-metal donation across the series. Population analysis derived from pre-bonding data rationalizes recent experimental X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) findings. Effective orbital overlaps extracted from XANES data using a simplified AO bonding model based on the Wolfsberg–Helmholtz (WH) relation are compared directly with pre-bonding overlaps. The consequences of using ionization potential (IP) based AO energies in the experimental data workup and other assumptions inherent in the bonding model are also scrutinized. Using consistent pre-bonding AO energies in the model requires a WH constant of 𝐾 ≃ 3 to reproduce the calculated overlaps for 4f-based interactions. Combining IP-based AO energies with a conventional value 𝐾 = 2, as done in prior studies, is shown to yield comparable overlaps due to a cancellation of errors. Overall, pre-bonding analysis provides a framework rooted in first-principles theory for connecting AO interactions in the molecule with experimental bonding trends.
items.authors: Kurtis Stanistreet-Welsh, Jacob A. Branson, Stefan G. Minasian, Jochen Autschbach
items.title_zh: [CeX6]2–（X = F, Cl, Br）中原子轨道相互作用的研究
items.summary_zh: 本文利用密度泛函理论（DFT）和预结合分析研究了[CeX6]2–复合物（X = F, Cl, Br）中的金属-配体键合。分析量化了复合物中原子轨道（AO）能量和重叠，重点关注铈（Ce）4f轨道与卤素𝑛p供体轨道之间的混合。结果表明，从F到Br，Ce-配体AO重叠的减少被AO能量匹配的改善所补偿，导致4f基的配体向金属的捐赠在系列中增加。基于预结合数据的种群分析合理化了近期实验的X射线吸收近边结构（XANES）发现。通过基于Wolfsberg-Helmholtz（WH）关系的简化AO结合模型从XANES数据中提取的有效轨道重叠与预结合重叠直接比较。使用基于电离势（IP）的AO能量在实验数据处理中的影响及模型固有假设也进行了审视。模型中使用一致的预结合AO能量需要WH常数𝐾 ≃ 3，以重现4f基相互作用的计算重叠。将基于IP的AO能量与传统值𝐾 = 2结合，显示出由于误差的抵消而产生可比的重叠。总体而言，预结合分析为连接AO提供了基于第一性原理理论的框架。

items.title: Influence of Structural Flexibility on Ion-Receptor Interactions in Octamethyl Calix[4]pyrrole Complexed with Prolinate
items.abstract: We present cryogenic ion vibrational spectroscopy of deprotonated L-proline ([Pro-H]-) complexed with octamethyl calix[4]pyrrole (omC4P). Density functional theory calculations reveal two low-energy binding motifs. In the lowest energy structure, the carboxylate group interacts with only three NH groups of omC4P, with the NH group of the fourth pyrrole pointing away from the binding site. In another geometry, slightly higher in energy, the ion binds to all four NH groups. The experimental IR spectrum matches the lowest energy isomer, featuring a free NH stretching signature at 3439 cm-1 alongside strongly red-shifted NH stretching modes involving the three strong hydrogen-bonding NH groups. This three-point binding motif represents a departure from the typical four-point binding observed with smaller anions, demonstrating how the charge distribution of the guest and the structural flexibility of the receptor affect binding of larger anions. Despite the reduced number of hydrogen bonds, the three-point binding motif is lower in energy due to shorter, stronger hydrogen bonds, and it is the dominant motif of [Pro-H]-·omC4P in vacuo.
items.authors: Lane M. Terry, J. Mathias Weber

items.title: Shaping Tumor Targeting: How Nanoparticle Morphology Influences Penetration and Accumulation in 3D Breast Cancer Models
items.abstract: Efficient nanomedicine delivery to solid tumors requires both tissue penetration and cellular accumulation, yet how nanocarrier architecture governs these processes remains poorly understood. Here, molecular polymer brushes spanning hydrodynamic radii (Rh) of 10–45 nm and aspect ratios of 1.2–8.1, with identical polysarcosine surface chemistry, are used to investigate transport in two extracellular matrix (ECM)-embedded breast cancer tumoroids: BT549 and MDA-MB-468 cells, separately. Passive transport reveals tumor entry as a major 2 barrier, while diffusion inside the tumoroid depends much less on particle morphology. While all particles enter the tumor spheroids, the smallest, near-spherical PeptoBrush (PB50, Rh = 10 nm) is the most efficient architecture for tumor penetration, which underlines that in an orientation of worm-like PeptoBrushes does not occur at the matrix tumor interphase under the experimental conditions. Functionalization of PB50 with an average of two cetuximab molecules strongly enhances EGFR-mediated tumor-cell association and accumulation while preserving deep tissue penetration. Time-resolved imaging reveals initial peripheral enrichment followed by progressive penetration toward the tumoroid core, consistent with a transient binding-site barrier. These findings distinguish two complementary determinants of intratumoral distribution in the extracellular matrix tumoroid model: nanocarrier morphology governs passive penetration, whereas antibody-mediated recognition drives cellular binding and tumoroid accumulation.
items.authors: Bonan Zhao, Michiel van Dijk, Anne van Gelder, Christine Seidl, Lin Jian, Kaloian Koynov

items.title: When the lower-barrier pathway yields the minor enantiomer: reversibility and intermediate stability in pyrroloindoline synthesis
items.abstract: In this work, we present a computational study that provides evidence for the origins of selectivity in the enantioselective synthesis of pyrroloindolines catalyzed by iminium ions. Through a conformational search combined with DFT calculations, we obtained the catalytic energy profile, which shows that the enantioselectivity is not determined by the barriers of the enantiodetermining C–C bond-forming step. A microkinetic model built on this profile reproduces the experimental enantiomeric excess and identifies the origin of the selectivity: under conditions in which the steps preceding product release are reversible, the catalyst-bound intermediate I9 accumulates preferentially along the S pathway, where it is markedly more stable than its R counterpart. The selectivity therefore reflects a thermodynamic contribution operating at the level of the diastereomeric on-cycle intermediates rather than a difference in activation barriers. We stress that this outcome is not accessible from the free energy profile alone: a simple inspection of the activation barriers predicts the opposite sense of induction, and only the explicit kinetic treatment reproduces the experimental results. Previous studies have suggested that control of the E/Z ratio of the iminium ion intermediate was related to catalytic selectivity; here we show that the stereoinduction originates from the predominance of the E isomer of the iminium ion. Furthermore, for the C–C bond-forming step, we identify the regions of the system involved in the noncovalent interactions that govern selectivity. Finally, by introducing substituents on the substrate, we observe a decrease in the activation barrier associated with the iminium ion–substrate interaction when electron-donating groups are present in the nucleophile.
items.authors: Felipe Schoma Cardoso, Bruno Matos Paz, Ataualpa A. C. Braga
items.title_zh: 低能垒路径导致少量对映体的原因研究
items.summary_zh: 本研究通过计算方法探讨了由亚胺离子催化的吡咯并吲哚类化合物的对映选择性来源。结合构象搜索与密度泛函理论（DFT）计算，我们获得了催化能量剖面，显示对映选择性并非由对映决定的C–C键形成步骤的能垒决定。基于该剖面的微动力学模型重现了实验中的对映过量，并确定了选择性的来源：在产品释放前的步骤可逆的条件下，催化剂结合的中间体I9沿S路径优先积累，其稳定性明显高于R对映体。因此，选择性反映的是在非对映体中间体层面上的热力学贡献，而非活化能垒的差异。我们强调，仅从自由能剖面无法获得这一结果：简单检查活化能垒预测了相反的诱导方向，只有显式的动力学处理才能重现实验结果。之前的研究表明，亚胺离子中间体的E/Z比的控制与催化选择性相关；本研究显示立体诱导源于S路径中间体的优势。

items.title: Enhancing Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction via Evolutionary Scale Modeling (ESM-2) and Hybrid Feature Integration
items.abstract: Experimental identification of B-cell epitopes is time-consuming and resource-intensive, motivating the adoption of computational prediction approaches. This study examines the progression of sequence-based strategies by contrasting traditional machine learning methods (SVM, XGBoost, etc.) and early deep learning techniques (CNN, RNN, etc.) with sophisticated protein language models such as ESM-2. By systematically evaluating multiple feature encodings, including amino acid composition, dipeptide composition, k-mer tokenization, and evolutionary embeddings, we established that capturing both global semantic context and local sequence motifs is essential for robust predictive performance. Optimal performance was achieved using a hybrid framework that combined 15B-parameter ESM-2 embeddings with k-mer features. This hybrid approach achieved an AUC of 0.743 and an MCC of 0.333 on independent validation using an Extra Trees classifier, and an AUC of 0.738 and an MCC of 0.356 using an XGBoost classifier on the same dataset. Our findings indicate that transformer-based embeddings yield enhanced protein representations; however, their predictive efficacy is optimized when integrated with local motifs and ensemble learning, presenting a scalable, high-accuracy alternative to conventional and standalone deep learning frameworks.
items.authors: Prasun Pal, Sai Jahnavi Pasumarthi, Sandipan Chakraborty

items.title: Black-Body-Based Scatter Removal Procedure for Quantitative Neutron Radiography at the MARS Beamline (CG-1D), HFIR
items.abstract: Quantitative neutron imaging is fundamentally limited by scattering artifacts, low neutron flux, and wavelength-dependent attenuation, which restrict accurate transmission measurements. This work presents the first implementation and validation of the blackbody (BB) based scatter removal procedure (Carminati et al., 2019) for quantitative neutron radiography of engineering materials at the MARS beamline (CG-1D), High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL). The scatter removal pipeline was applied to a series of single crystal nickel (Ni) and polycrystalline austenitic (γ-phase) 316L stainless steel samples pre-charged with hydrogen gas (H2) at pressures of 1.5, 5, 12.5, and 20 kpsi. The BB correction removed a spatially varying scatter contribution of up to 8% of the local transmission that was not eliminated by conventional open-beam normalization. After scatter removal and subtraction of the metal-matrix attenuation, the resulting H attenuation coefficient, µH, increased monotonically with H concentration in both materials. Ni exhibited a higher H attenuation response than 316L stainless steel, consistent with differences in H solubility and trapping behavior. Pixel-wise maps further revealed concentration-dependent spatial heterogeneity, including localized regions of elevated µH in Ni at the highest H concentration. At the lowest concentrations, uncertainty in the interpolated scatter field exceeded the spatial-sampling uncertainty and established the effective detection floor of the measurement. Independent validation experiments were performed at the VENUS beamline of the Spallation Neutron Source using a H-free 316L stainless steel sample as a control and a water column with a known H number density as a reference standard. The corrected measurements recovered the expected zero H signal in the control and the H attenuation of the water reference, demonstrating that the pipeline can distinguish H attenuation from matrix and scatter contributions across independent beamline conditions. These results establish a validated workflow for removing sample dependent scatter and enabling quantitative analysis of neutron radiography data acquired at cold-neutron imaging beamlines.
items.authors: Dayeeta Pal, James Torres, Yuxuan Zhang, Hassina Bilheux, Jean-Christophe Bilheux, Zipeng Xu

items.title: Why Molecular-Scale Occupancy Fluctuations Appear Gaussian without Being Bulk-Like
items.abstract: Molecular-scale occupancy distributions in water and hard-sphere fluids can appear remarkably Gaussian. Using classical density functional theory with an external field conjugate to the occupancy, we calculate occupancy cumulants for spherical volumes in a hard-sphere fluid and reproduce the variance and small, oscillatory third moment reported previously in Monte Carlo simulations. This agreement shows that the density functional captures the correlations responsible for the phenomenon and allows the role of excluded-volume packing to be isolated. By comparison with the Poisson limit and by varying both observation-volume size and bulk density, we show that excluded-volume correlations strongly suppress the higher cumulants. The resulting skewness and excess kurtosis remain nonzero and oscillatory, but they become small as the observation volume increases. However, over the same molecular-scale range, the finite-volume variance remains strongly scale-dependent and does not attain the extensive scaling set by the bulk compressibility. The early onset of near-Gaussianity is therefore governed primarily by molecular packing: it does not demonstrate that the fluctuations have reached the thermodynamic Gaussian limit, nor does it support a distinct small-cavity regime governed by bulk-like Gaussian fluctuations.
items.authors: Nigel B. Wilding
items.title_zh: 分子尺度占据波动为何呈高斯分布而非体相特征
items.summary_zh: 水和硬球流体中的分子尺度占据分布可以表现出显著的高斯特征。我们使用经典密度泛函理论，结合与占据相关的外场，计算了硬球流体中球形体积的占据累积量，并重现了之前蒙特卡洛模拟中报告的方差和小的振荡三阶矩。这一结果表明，密度泛函捕捉了导致该现象的相关性，并使排斥体积效应得以分离。通过与泊松极限的比较以及改变观察体积和体密度，我们发现排斥体积相关性显著抑制了高阶累积量。最终的偏度和超峰度保持非零且振荡，但随着观察体积的增大而减小。然而，在相同的分子尺度范围内，有限体积方差仍然强烈依赖于尺度，并未达到由体积压缩性设定的广泛标度。因此，近高斯性的早期出现主要受分子堆积的控制，并不表明波动已达到热力学高斯极限，也不支持由体相高斯波动主导的小腔体制。

items.title: Chemical Synthesis of the endogenous metabolite Phosphocitrate and Its Structural Isomer Phosphoisocitrate
items.authors: Petri Turhanen

items.title: QM_eMMa: An Open GPU-Accelerated Framework for Ab Initio QM/MM Molecular Dynamics and Enhanced Sampling
items.abstract: Ab initio QM/MM molecular dynamics can describe chemical processes accurately, but its practical use is limited by the cost of repeated electronic-structure calculations and by overhead in coupling molecular-dynamics and quantum-chemistry programs. We present QM_eMMa, an open interface that couples AMBER to PySCF/GPU4PySCF while keeping the electronic-structure engine and GPU context active throughout a simulation. The converged electronic density is reused between consecutive MD steps, with automatic recovery through a cold-start SCF calculation when needed. We first optimized the workflow with a GH125 α-mannosidase model. Removing repeated interface overhead increased throughput by approximately 26%. Systematic energy and force comparisons then identified a less expensive numerical setting that retained the accuracy required for MD and increased throughput by a further 23% in independent GH125 simulations. The same protocol enabled stable DFT/MM dynamics of a larger enzymatic QM region containing 115 electronic centers and sustained 145 ps of ab initio well-tempered metadynamics, recovering the principal α-mannose conformational basins observed previously. Finally, a reactive aqueous SN2 benchmark showed that the optimized and stricter protocols gave activation and reaction free energies differing by only 0.73 and 0.01 kcal mol-1, respectively, while the optimized calculation remained faster. QM_eMMa therefore provides a practical open framework for single-GPU DFT/MM dynamics and enhanced sampling, with numerical approximations selected through explicit validation of energies, forces, dynamics, and chemical reactivity.
items.authors: Santiago Alonso-Gil

items.title: A theory of inner-sphere reorganization energy for electrocatalysis
items.abstract: In Marcus theory, reorganization energy links thermodynamics and kinetics for outer-sphere electron transfer, in which the redox centre exchanges an electron without changing its bonding to the electrode. Most electrocatalytic elementary steps are instead inner-sphere processes: the reacting intermediate is part of the interface, and surface bonding changes with charge transfer. A general thermodynamic definition of the full nonequilibrium preparation cost of such a bonded interface is lacking, leaving equilibrium descriptors and measured rates without a common theoretical basis. Here we define this quantity thermodynamically and provide a first-principles procedure for its calculation. A Legendre transform of fixed-potential thermodynamics yields an internal free-energy surface in which interfacial polarization and surface bond state are coupled variables, while electrode potential remains an external control. For a specified elementary event, inner-sphere reorganization energy is the finite free-energy cost of preparing a product-like interface before relaxation. Writing this cost as a Bregman difference separates it from the reaction driving force and relates it to a weighted integral of local interfacial stiffness. The classical Marcus expression is recovered as the one-dimensional harmonic charge-only limit of this framework. Applied to Volmer hydrogen oxidation on
items.authors: Kaicong Yang, Bing Huang, Lin Zhuang

items.title: Why Electrochemical–Thermal–Mechanical Understanding is Needed to Explain Knees in Lithium-Ion Batteries Degradation
items.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are essential to modern life, spanning portable electronics, electric vehicles and grid storage. Yet, their degradation mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly the sudden capacity drops known as knee points. In this study, commercial Samsung 50S cells are degraded under various cooling setups and charge/discharge rates, revealing consistent knees in slow-discharge cells even above 80% of initial capacity, while fast-discharge cells degraded beyond 60% without knees. Using a multiphysics characterisation approach, we decipher the origins of these knees: attainment of lower voltages enhances silicon activity, triggering a chain of mechanisms that culminate in sudden failure. Specifically, recurring SEI reformation drives a dual pathway: gas release displaces electrolyte, inducing localised current concentration, overcharge and a first pattern of lithium plating, while simultaneous electrode thickening deforms the jelly roll. This mechanical effect, combined with geometrical heterogeneities from the welded tab design, produces a second pattern of lithium plating in later ageing states, identified as the primary cause of the knees. These findings elucidate the complex coupling of multiscale degradation mechanisms and demonstrate that robust state-of-health monitoring must be holistic, incorporating indicators beyond traditional temperature, capacity and resistance.
items.authors: Matheus Leal de Souza, M. Waseem Marzook, Mohammed Asheruddin N, Derek Siu, Antonis Vamvakeros, Gregory Offer

items.title: Reducing Synthetic Complexity: A Fluorine-Free Benzodithiophene-Thienopyrrolodione Donor Polymer by Direct Arylation Polycondensation for Organic Photovoltaics
items.abstract: Synthetic complexity is a decisive aspect for absorber material availability in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). By using direct arylation polycondensation (DAP), a new route to the donor polymer PBDT-T2-TPD is presented. DAP allows to reduce the amount of toxic chemicals and simplifies the reaction scheme at the same time. Furthermore, this new route allows to vary the molar mass of PBDT-T2-TPD and thus enables the investigation of chain length-dependent OPV parameters in devices with the non-fullerene L8-BO as acceptor. An increasing molar mass results in an improvement of the open-circuit voltage, the fill factor and the power conversion efficiency, while the short-circuit current density saturates after an initial increase. items.authors: Christian Biebl, Maria Saladina, Chen Wang, Pooja Pandey, Carsten Deibel, Michael Sommer

items.title: Zeolite-Mediated Three- and Pseudo-Five-Component Reactions Involving α-Ketoglutaric Acid, Aromatic Aldehydes and 5-Aminotetrazole
items.abstract: We report previously undescribed multicomponent reactions of α-ketoglutaric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 5-aminotetrazole that provides access to two distinct types of products. Notably, these transformations require the presence of 4A or 3A molecular sieves, and the formation of the target compounds is condition-controllable: the process can proceed through a pseudo-five-component pathway, yielding tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidinone derivatives – the first examples of this heterocyclic framework – or can be directed toward a three-component condensation that affords dihydrotetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine dicarboxylic acids. The latter were identified as key intermediates in the pseudo-five-component transformation, enabling the synthesis of pyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidine systems via a two-step Doebner-type and Castagnoli–Cushman-type/decarboxylation sequence with an expanded range of possible substrates, thereby combining tetrazole, dihydropyrimidine, δ-lactam, and triazole pharmacophore motifs within a single fused framework.
items.authors: Vladyslav O. Honcharov, Valentyn A. Chebanov, Olena H. Shvets, Vyacheslav E. Saraev, Svitlana V. Shishkina, Yana I. Sakhno

items.title: Aged Hops Increase 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol (MBT), β-Ionone, and Branched-Chain Esters in Beer
items.authors: Toru KISHIMOTO

items.title: Macromolecular Size Matching in Stabilizing Corrugated Chiral Plasmonic Nanostructures
items.abstract: Chiral plasmonic nanoparticles derive strong chiroptical responses sensitive from their corrugated, high-curvature surfaces, but these same features are thermodynamically unstable. Surface functionalization using macromolecules could broaden their utility by enabling improved colloidal compatibility, secondary functionalization, stimuli responsiveness and and assembly into higher-order structures. However, as the chiroptically active surface feactures are often only a few nanometer in size, inadequate size matching leads to structural instability, causing particle surfaces to flatten and consequently diminishing their chiroptical properties. Here, we show that chain-length-selective polymer functionalization stabilizes the fine groove structures of chiral gold nanorods. We identify a threshold behavior of hydrodynamic diameter below which polymer coils can penetrate and anchor within the grooves, preserving structural integrity and chiroptical activities. Guided by this principle, we establish a sequential functionalization strategy using polymers of two distinct sizes to produce chiral AuNRs with stable chiroptical performance. Our results establish a general design rule for integrating versatile macromolecular architectures with chiral nanoparticles and expand the engineering space for nano-optical applications.
items.authors: Yingying Cai, Anjana Kannan, Jessica Ma, Qun Song, Yuwen Peng, Kai Zhang

items.title: A bench-scale, continuous reactor for reductive polyolefin depolymerization
items.abstract: Catalytic deconstruction of polyolefins is central to chemical recycling, but most laboratory studies use batch reactors that obscure kinetics and limit reproducibility. Flow operation enables rigorous measurement of rates and selectivities, yet processing viscous polymer melts at small scales remains challenging. Here we present a laboratory-scale flow reactor that couples a hydraulic melt pump to a stirred-tank vessel, enabling continuous and semi-continuous operation at high pressure. The system achieves pseudo-steady state, where volatile production rates reflect C–C scission kinetics, validated by a first-principles model. Using this reactor with H-ZSM-5, we demonstrate three features of polyethylene hydrocracking difficult to probe in batch systems, namely that alkene selectivities exceed batch reactions by nearly tenfold, hydrogen availability within the melt governs the balance between alkene and alkane products, and catalyst acidity and crystallite size jointly tune this product balance through intermediate diffusion from the zeolite. This reactor provides a platform for kinetic and mechanistic studies of catalytic polymer deconstruction.
items.authors: Griffin Drake, Juliana Lu-Yang, Anna E. Brenner, Joel Miscall, Gregg T. Beckham, Yuriy Román-Leshkov

items.title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
items.abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts. Enamides readily undergo catalyst-free intramolecular [3+2] cycloaddition under mild conditions to afford the previously unknown 3,3a,4-trisubstituted-3a,4-dihydro-3 H -imidazo[1,2-c][1,2,3]triazol-5(6 H )-one scaffold in high yields. This novel fused heterocyclic system was fully characterised and proved to be a highly versatile intermediate for divergent post -Ugi transformations. Fused dihydrotriazoles transformed into 3,5-dihydroimidazol-4-ones via an elimination of N 2 supplemented by acylamide migration. Additionally, base- or acid-mediated cascades enabled efficient one-pot access to aromatised 1,2,3-triazoles and open-chain triamides, respectively. In total, 4 generations of structural isomers and 2 other classes of compounds were involved in the work. The methodologies developed highlight the synthetic value of azido-modified enamides as divergent intermediates, providing rapid and controlled entry to structurally diverse nitrogen-rich heterocycles and peptidomimetics from simple Ugi adducts derived from α , β- unsaturated aldehydes.
items.authors: Vladyslav Vereshchak, Viacheslav Saraiev, Vladimir Musatov, Svitlana Shishkina, Valentyn Chebanov, Alexander Tsygankov

items.title: Quantifying Validation-Induced Optimism in Machine Learning for Food Spectroscopy: An Empirical Multi-Dataset Benchmark
items.abstract: Background: Evaluating machine-learning regression models in food spectroscopy using random row-wise cross-validation ignores hierarchical experimental structures (replicate scans, aliquot extractions, packaging batches, instruments, and harvest campaigns). While theoretical warnings caution against sample leakage, the chemometric literature lacks a multidataset empirical quantification of validation-induced optimism, its impact on model selection, and its underlying physical mechanisms. Methods: We executed an empirical multi-dataset benchmark across four benchmark food spectroscopy collections encompassing 12,706 source spectra/records, with 6,376 spectra evaluated in primary regression workflows: Cargill corn near-infrared (NIR; n = 240 spectra across 80 physical grain samples and 3 spectrometers; targets: moisture and protein), edible vegetable oils Raman (Gilbraith , 2024; n = 215 spectra across 52 distinct reference titration determinations; target: peroxide value), mango fruit dry matter NIR (Anderson , 2020; n = 4,233 calibration spectra across 5 cultivars and n = 1,448 external harvest season spectra; target: dry matter content), and Tecator meat NIR (n = 240 spectra with 24 duplicate pairs [48 rows participating in identical pairs], leaving 216 unique spectral profiles; targets: fat and moisture). Six regression algorithms—partial least squares (PLS), Ridge regression, support vector regression (SVR-RBF), Random Forest, XGBoost, and k-nearest neighbours (kNN, serving as a diagnostic sentinel)—were evaluated across four hierarchical validation tiers: Level 1 (random row-wise cross-validation), Level 2 (sample-aware group cross-validation, reference-valuegrouped validation, or deduplicated validation), Level 3 (cultivar-aware validation), and Level 4 (external instrument and seasonal holdout). Model specifications were held fixed across validation tiers to isolate validation design as the sole manipulated factor, and all spectral standardisation was strictly fitted within training partitions to eliminate unsupervised leakage. Results: Transitioning from random row-wise to structured validation systematically eroded apparent predictive performance across all 36 random-to-structured model–task contrasts, yielding a median validation-induced optimism ΔR2 of 0.0170 (mean 0.3290, interquartile range [0.0084, 0.3985]) and a median root-mean-square error inflation ratio (RR_RMSE = RMSE_structured / RMSE_random) of 1.1395 (mean 1.4277, IQR [1.0417, 1.4374], range [0.9406, 5.2645]). Degradation was especially pronounced under external domain transfer (median ΔR2 = 0.6399, median RR_RMSE = 1.8199). In edible oils containing replicate scans sharing identical titration reference values, random cross-validation produced catastrophic performance inflation for non-linear models: kNN collapsed from an apparent R2 of 0.8865 (RMSE 5.40 meq O2/kg) to −2.1443 (RMSE 28.43 meq O2/kg; RR_RMSE = 5.265), and Random Forest collapsed from R2 = 0.8437 to −0.5806 (RR_RMSE = 3.180). This replicate leakage completely inverted algorithm rankings (Spearman ρ = −0.886, p = 0.019; Kendall τ = −0.733, p = 0.056). Algorithm robustness under external transfer was domain-specific: Ridge was the most resilient model under Mango seasonal transfer (R2 = 0.6690, compared to R2 ≈ 0.13–0.17 for tree ensembles), whereas uncalibrated Corn instrument transfer caused severe degradation in linear models (Ridge R2 = −30.04, PLS R2 = −37.05) due to uncorrected spectrometer baseline shifts. In contrast, non-linear models exhibited smaller relative degradation under sensor transfer. Cross-partition nearest-neighbour spectral similarity dropped by up to 0.0164 under domain transfer. Across tasks, this similarity drop showed an exploratory positive association with kNN error inflation (Pearson r = 0.739, Spearman ρ = 0.912), consistent with a spectral-proximity mechanism whereby high optical similarity enables flexible models to interpolate training points rather than learning transferable chemical relationships. Conclusions: Random row-wise validation creates severe validation-induced optimism, distorts algorithm rankings, and rewards models that memorise experimental artefacts. Reporting standards, mandatory specimen-level split manifests, and the routine inclusion of kNN as a diagnostic canary are essential to restore methodological integrity and field deployability to machine learning in food analysis.
items.authors: Ketney Otto

items.title: Crowding-induced interfacial aggregation underlies enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition during poly(ethylene terephthalate) depolymerization
items.abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) using PET hydrolases (PETases) offers a sustainable route for plastic recycling, yet high enzyme loadings paradoxically reduce degradation efficiency. The molecular basis of this enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition (ECDI) has remained unresolved. Here, by exploiting host-dependent differences in folding quality of a sequence-identical PETase, we show that ECDI is driven by crowding-induced interfacial aggregation, which progressively destabilizes PET-bound enzymes. By establishing aggregation propensity as a tractable design parameter, we demonstrate a complementary multi-level engineering framework operating at the sequence, folding, and reaction-environment levels that suppresses interfacial aggregation and improves PET depolymerization across multiple PETases. Our findings reveal how enzyme–enzyme interactions can govern catalytic performance at heterogeneous solid–liquid interfaces, providing a mechanistic basis for designing high-performance biocatalytic systems under high-enzyme-loading conditions.
items.authors: Eon Ji Jo, Byung Hoon Jo

items.title: Transferable Graph Neural Network Surrogates for Molecular Dynamics Across Crystal Symmetries
items.abstract: We present a transferable graph neural network (GNN) surrogate framework for molecular dynamics (MD) that directly predicts atomic displacements and propagates atomistic configurations without explicit force evaluation or numerical time integration. The central objective of this work is to establish whether a common GNN formulation can represent atomic dynamics across materials with fundamentally different crystal symmetries and coordination environments. The same network architecture, feature representation, graph construction, and training protocol are applied without symmetry-specific modification to face-centered cubic (FCC) aluminum, body-centered cubic (BCC) iron, and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) magnesium. Across these distinct elemental and crystallographic systems, the framework achieves position-prediction errors on the order of 10−4 Å 2 and supports stable autoregressive propagation to nanosecond time scales. The predicted trajectories preserve thermodynamic stability, characteristic coordination-shell structure in the radial distribution functions, and temperature-dependent mean-squared-displacement behavior. In particular, the framework captures the closely spaced coordination shells of BCC iron and the anisotropic coordination environment of HCP magnesium without introducing lattice-specific representations. These results demonstrate that direct GNN-based atomic propagation can be formulated as a transferable framework across different elements, lattice symmetries, and coordination geometries, providing a pathway toward generalizable surrogate models for accelerated molecular dynamics.
items.authors: Judah Immanuel, Avik Mahata, Aniruddha Maiti

items.title: Electrochemically Hole-catalyzed Dearomative (3+2) Cycloaddition of Nitroarenes
items.abstract: We report the first electrochemically hole-catalyzed (3+2) dearomative cycloaddition of nitroarenes, including benzene-based derivatives. Enabled by a hole-transfer chain process, the reaction proceeds through the anodic generation of a non-stabilized azomethine ylide from a readily available precursor, providing efficient access to structurally complex pyrrolidines from a broad range of electron-deficient nitroarenes. Remarkably, full conversion is achieved using catalytic amounts of electricity (0.1 F mol-1), resulting in high TONe (222) and Faradaic efficiency (925%). This work expands the scope of hole electrocatalysis beyond electron-rich olefins and establishes a new platform for electrochemical dearomative cycloadditions. The scalability of the method was further demonstrated under continuous-flow conditions.
items.authors: Nathan Noël, Youssou Faye, Julien Legros, Laëtitia Chausset-Boissarie, Isabelle Chataigner

items.title: Fiber-Scale Discrete Element Modeling Approach for Microstructural Evolution in Carbon Felt Electrode Manufacturing
items.abstract: Porous carbon components strongly influence transport, kinetics, and performance in electrochemical energy devices, like electrodes in redox flow batteries or gas diffusion layers in proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Yet quantitative links between industrial felt manufacturing and the resulting microstructure remain insufficiently understood. Recent studies have explored alternative bottom-up fabrication strategies to achieve greater microstructural control, while computational optimization often considers stochastic microstructures without accounting for manufacturability. Consequently, the extent to which conventional manufacturing processes can tailor microstructure remains unclear. Here, we develop a discrete element method framework that resolves fiber-scale interactions and microstructural evolution during mechanical processing of oxidized polyacrylonitrile precursor felts. The framework represents successive stages of fiber generation, web formation, web laying, needle punching, and calendering. At each stage, the evolving three-dimensional microstructure is resolved and quantified using fiber- and pore-scale descriptors, including pore-size distributions, fiber-orientation tensors, and transport-related properties. The simulations reveal process–structure–transport relationships, identifying key parameters governing pore-throat size, fiber reorientation, and effective diffusivity. These findings define the microstructural design space accessible through conventional felt manufacturing and provide a basis for future process optimization and integration with subsequent thermal-processing stages.
items.authors: Arjun Sankar, Abhilash Valisammagari, Francisco Fernandez, Alejandro A. Franco

items.title: A conformational filter protocol for structures with topological symmetry
items.abstract: This paper presents an efficient conformational filter protocol for handling structures with topological symmetry implemented in the open-source molecular modelling program curcuma. This approach addresses the challenge of comparing molecular conformations in which symmetrically equivalent atoms may have different indices in the structure files. Descriptors that are independent of the storing order of the atoms (energy differences, rotational constants, and Vietoris-Rips (VR) persistence barcodes) are used to efficiently predict potential structural similarities before performing computationally expensive permutations on selected structure pairs using distinct permutation approaches implemented in curcuma or the external tool molalign. The filter protocol operates in three phases: 1) initial RMSD-based filtering and data-set-specific training of the atom index-independent descriptor thresholds, 2) permutation-based filtering using parameterised descriptors, and 3) final filtering using stored permutation vectors. Our evaluation using 395 complex conformations optimised at different levels of theory shows that although conformational geometries typically remain similar across different theoretical methods; their relative energies can vary significantly between different levels of theory. This highlights the importance of efficient conformational filtering in identifying structurally unique conformers, particularly when faster semiempirical quantum chemical methods are used, which might incorrectly evaluate certain conformers as energetically unfavourablein contrast to slower more accurate quantum mechinal methods. A key finding is that performing all possible RMSD calculations does not necessarily yield the optimal filtering result, as the final outcome depends significantly on the specific order of the structure comparisons.
items.authors: Conrad Hübler

items.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics-Informed Machine Learning-Enabled Digital Twin for Vapor Maldistribution Prediction in Structured Packed Distillation Columns
items.abstract: Vapor maldistribution in structured-packed distillation columns reduces separation performance. While experimental measurements are essential for characterizing column hydrodynamics, they often lack the resolution to capture velocity distributions or to systematically quantify how column geometry and operating conditions affect vapor maldistribution throughout the packed bed. High-fidelity, first-principles computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations can provide detailed spatial flow information, but their high computational cost limits the rapid evaluation of alternative column designs and operating conditions. To address this limitation, a CFD-informed machine-learning (ML) reduced-order model (ROM) framework was developed to rapidly predict vapor flow uniformity in structured-packed distillation columns. 3D CFD simulations were performed for 13 column geometries by varying column diameter, inlet diameter, nozzle-to-packing clearance, and vapor mass flow rate, yielding a dataset of 65 simulation cases for parametric analysis and ML model training. Vapor maldistribution was quantified using the area-weighted coefficient of variation (CoV) of streamwise velocity across 13 packing layers. CFD results indicated that vapor maldistribution was most pronounced near the packed-bed entrance and progressively decreased through the packing. Higher vapor flow rates and smaller inlet diameters generally increased maldistribution in the inletdominated region, while the effect of nozzle-to-packing clearance depended on column geometry and scale. For instance, increasing the inlet diameter reduced the Layer-1 CoV from 51.01% to 30.73% in the 47.75-in. column and from 48.82% to 22.32% in the 120in. column. A Gaussian process regression (GPR)-based ROM was subsequently trained using the CFD dataset and evaluated through leave-one-geometry-out cross-validation. Across 65 held-out cases and 845 packed-layer predictions, the ROM achieved a mean absolute error of 0.851, a root mean squared error of 1.524, and a coefficient of determination of 0.980. Prediction errors were primarily concentrated in the lower packing layers, where the flow was strongly influenced by the inlet geometry, and decreased substantially farther downstream. The resulting CFD-informed ML framework offers a computationally efficient digital-twin development workflow for predicting vapor maldistribution in previously untested column geometries and, within the investigated design space, enables rapid geometry screening and design optimization of structuredpacked distillation columns.
items.authors: Alek Nino, Hang Yi, Tony Cai, Izak Nieuwoudt, Yu Feng

items.title: Quality control measurement science: Point-of-care opioid compounding and personalized pain management
items.abstract: Traditional "one-size-fits-all" pharmacotherapy often fails to address the complex, highly individualized needs of patients undergoing opioid tapering, pain management, and withdrawal. While distributed and point-of-care (POC) additive manufacturing—such as 3D printing, semisolid extrusion, and drop-on-demand (DoD) deposition—enable agile, patient-specific dosing and multi-drug formulations, they introduce critical quality control (QC) challenges in facilities that often lack extensive laboratory infrastructure. We employed a quality by design (QbD) approach to identify the critical relationships between input materials, process parameters, and critical quality attributes (CQAs) and investigated a tiered series of atline, inline, and final-product QC measurement technologies for personalized pain management and opioid-tapering therapies. Using precision DoD liquid dispensers, various tunable dosage forms were produced, including injectable saline solutions, semi-solid extruded tablets, and oral films. These vehicles carried full and partial opioid agonists, opioid antagonists, and adjuvant withdrawal medications (fentanyl, buprenorphine, methadone, oxycodone, naloxone, diphenhydramine, promethazine, and 2 bupivacaine). The performance, speed, and selectivity of four analytical techniques were explored: microdrop UV-Vis spectroscopy, liquid chromatography-UV (LC-UV), handheld Raman spectroscopy, and chromatography-free direct analysis in real time triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (DART-TQ-MS). We characterized and quantified each manufactured dosage form by either single-point calibration (i.e., against a reference standard [RS] or quality control standard) or linear least squares regression. Analytical control strategies for quality control require balancing throughput, analytical capabilities and limitations, and specific medicine considerations. This work defined robust metrological pathways for safe, compliant, and personalized point-ofcare pharmaceutical production, bridging clinical pain management and opioid tapering guidelines with manufacturing quality assurance.
items.authors: Thomas P. Forbes, Zainab Altamimi, Jeffrey Lawrence, Elizabeth L. Robinson

items.title: In-situ Electrochemical Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Characterization of Polymer and MXene Films
items.abstract: In-situ electrochemical spectroscopic ellipsometry (EC-SE) can enable real-time monitoring of optical properties and thickness changes of surfaces and thin films. This method can provide a broad range of information on the evolution of the microenvironment of an electrode during electrochemical reactions. However, to avoid modeling artifacts, accurate data analysis is critical. Here, we outline key steps in data analysis that can help prevent overfitting and misinterpretation of results. For example, determining the refractive index of the electrolyte at the air/electrolyte interface, along with measurements of the electrode’s dielectric data in dry conditions, can yield more accurate results than simultaneous fitting of all parameters for the electrolyte and electrode. We also present detailed modeling strategies tailored to fitting in-situ cyclic voltammetry (CV) data on various types of thin films, by providing two distinct examples: the thickness change of catalyst polymer films due to swelling by the electrolyte, and the simultaneous change in thickness and optical properties of Ti3C2Tx MXene films due to both reversible (electrochromic effect) and irreversible (degradation) processes. These details can help guide the informed selection of models in similar conditions by providing practical guidelines. The step-by-step approach to modeling can be more broadly adopted to enhance the accuracy and reproducibility of EC-SE experiments for interfacial studies relevant to energy conversion and storage, as well as other electrochemical reactions.
items.authors: Hui Fang, Manushree Tanwar, Hannah S. Nedzbala, Anupma Thakur, Sophia LaPorta, Howe Chen

items.title: Neutron Crystallography Maps the Interaction Landscape of Pseudomonas aeruginosa LecA with Deuterated Aromatic β-Galactoside
items.abstract: Aromatic derivatives of β-galactosides are potent inhibitors of the LecA lectin, a key virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, involved in host recognition, tissue adhesion and biofilm formation. This opportunistic bacterial pathogen is considered a serious global health threat, particularly due to the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains. Anti-adhesive and anti-biofilm compounds represent promising alternatives or complements to conventional antibiotic therapies. The design of such pathoblockers requires detailed structural insights into their interactions with the target protein. Neutron macromolecular crystallography (NMX) provides complementary structural information to X-ray diffraction (XRD), by enabling the localization of hydrogen atoms, but typically requires the use of deuterium-labeled molecules. We developed a unique approach combining bacterial production of deuterated galactose and its functionalization with a deuterated phenyl group, resulting in the first synthesis of perdeuterated phenyl-β-galactoside, PheβGal-d16. The structure of the deuterated bacterial receptor LecA in complex with PheβGal-d16 was determined using neutron diffraction, providing experimental localization of hydrogen atoms involved in hydrophobic contacts with the Pro38 and Gln53 residues, and in the unusual T-shaped π-stacking interaction with His50. These observations rationalize the 10-fold affinity increase measured for an aromatic β-galactoside compared to galactose.
items.authors: Theodore Arnaud, Delphine Carry, Chloé Tatol, Juliette M. Devos, Lukas Gajdos, Philippe Lesot

items.title: Strategic Bromine Substitution in Aryl Aminoboranes Unlocks Photochemical Route to Narrow-Band Emitting Azaborines
items.abstract: The development of UV/deep-blue emitters with high color purity remains a central challenge in OLED research, where conventional fluorophores suffer from broad emission and triplet-harvesting systems compromise stability. Here we show that strategic ortho-bromine substitution in bis-aryl aminoboranes unlocks an intramolecular photo-cyclization that allows direct access to azaborine frameworks under mild conditions and near quantitative yield. The high triplet energy of the aminoborane precursors enables efficient population of the T1 state, triggering ring closure and suppressing the twisted intramolecular charge-transfer (TICT) behavior characteristic of the open scaffolds. The resulting azaborines display deep-blue to near-UV emission, with remarkably narrow bandwidths (FWHM down to 0.09 eV in solution and 0.04 eV in glassy matrix) and localized excited states (LE). A systematic library screening unveils the modularity of this approach and shows that cyclization rate correlate with spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and triplet-state localization on the B-N bond. This work establishes the first photochemical route to azaborines and provides a synthetically versatile platform for high-purity emitters, suited for next-generation optoelectronic applications.
items.authors: Alessio Bussolari, Nunzio Matera, Andrea Pellegrini, Nicolò Mazzini, Sven Reese, Wojciech Mróz

items.title: Fracture mechanics favors lower-than-expected stack pressures in halide solidstate batteries
items.abstract: All-solid-state batteries promise safer, more energy-dense storage than cells built on liquid electrolytes. Among solid-state electrolytes, halide electrolytes offer high ionic conductivity, anodic stability, and room-temperature processability, yet stable cycling is typically achieved under stack pressures of tens to hundreds of megapascals, for reasons that remain unclear. Here we identify the unusually high susceptibility of brittle halide electrolytes to fracture as the mechanism underlying and show that stack pressure—conventionally applied to suppress mechanical damage—can instead promote it by enhancing strain transfer from the active materials to the surrounding electrolyte. Operando scanning electron microscopy captures crack initiation and propagation within electrolyte domains in composite cathodes driven by active material volume changes, while nanoindentation reveals an exceptionally low fracture toughness of 0.23 MPa·m1/2 for the representative halide electrolyte Li3YCl6, substantially lower than the 0.7−1.0 MPa·m1/2 for typical sulfide and oxide electrolytes. Pressure-dependent electrochemical and morphological analyses show that, although modest pressure is sufficient to maintain interparticle contact, increasing pressure beyond this level promotes electrolyte fracture and accelerates capacity loss. Guided by this insight, we demonstrate an anode-free halide pouch cell that retains 85% of its capacity over 200 cycles at C/3 under only 2 MPa. Together, these findings show that the high stack pressures widely used in halide solid-state batteries primarily compensate for the consequences of electrolyte fracture rather than reflecting the pressure intrinsically required for stable operation, establishing a mechanical basis for low-pressure halide solid-state batteries.
items.authors: Liqun Guo, Jie Zheng, Lihong Zhao, Santosh Thapa, Yanliang Liang, Phat Tieu

items.title: Helical Polymers for Artificial Cell Engineering: Backbone-to-Droplet Reorganization in Polyacetylene-based Microdroplets
items.abstract: Biomolecular condensates provide a powerful framework for constructing artificial cells with crowded interiors and dynamic molecular organization. However, most synthetic condensates rely on flexible or intrinsically disordered macromolecules, leaving the role of conformationally defined synthetic polymers in liquid-liquid phase separation largely unexplored. Here, we introduce cationic helical polyacetylenes as structurally defined building blocks for coacervate-based artificial cells and investigate how their conformation governs condensate properties. Complexation with ATP generates spherical, liquid-like microdroplets that sequester small organic molecules and proteins from the surrounding solution while supporting enzymatic transformations. These coacervates exhibit substantially greater resistance to increasing ionic strength than those formed with their linear counterparts, a behavior associated with changes in the polyacetylene backbone upon ATP complexation. Moreover, combining helical and linear polyamines induces the heterogeneous partitioning of a hydrophilic molecular guest, accompanied by a transition from spherical to amorphous condensates. Together, these findings establish a direct link between polymer secondary structure and condensate stability, morphology, and molecular organization, highlighting conformationally defined synthetic polymers as versatile building blocks for artificial cell engineering.
items.authors: Bruno Delgado Gonzalez, Ivan Torreiro-Leon, Lucía Medín-Agraso, Lorena Sánchez-Domínguez, Manuel Míguez, Roberto J. Brea

items.title: Additive manufacturing of micro-architected carbide ceramics via molten salt conversion
items.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables complex micro-architected geometries in metals 1–3 , polymers 4 and oxide ceramics 4–6 , yet its extension to non-oxide ceramics remains constrained by optical opacity and high-temperature densification. Carbide ceramics are challenging for particle-based vat photopolymerization (VPP), where strong absorption limits curing, while pressure-assisted densification, often required for high density, is incompatible with delicate architectures. A general route to fabricate dense micro-architected carbide ceramics without conventional sintering remains unavailable. Here we demonstrate molten salt-assisted additive manufacturing of carbide ceramics (MOSAIC), an AM framework that decouples geometric shaping from carbide formation. Thermoset polymer architectures fabricated by VPP are pyrolysed into architected glassy-carbon templates and converted into carbide ceramics through molten-salt-mediated reaction with transition metals. MOSAIC produces micro-architected TiC, VC, Cr 3 C 2 and TaC with relative densities above 95% and features down to ~20 µm, and extends to WC, ZrC and Mo 2 C. Conversion depth can be controlled from ~1 µm to tens of micrometres, yielding solid carbide struts or hollow architectures after carbon removal. Controlled oxidation converts these structures into TiO 2 , Cr 2 O 3 , V 2 O 5 and Ta 2 O 5 while preserving topology. By separating architecture definition from ceramic formation, MOSAIC enables photopolymerization-based manufacturing of transition-metal carbides and derivative oxides across micrometre-scale features and millimetre- to centimetre-scale architectures.
items.authors: Chiranjit Roy, Apurv Dash

items.title: A Vanadium(II) Photosensitizer Delivered by Human Serum Albumin for Photodynamic Therapy
items.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an established clinically approved treatment; however, the development of next-generation photosensitizers remains constrained by the reliance on scarce precious-metal scaffolds and poor pharmacological properties. Earth-abundant first-row transition metals offer an attractive alternative, but their application in PDT remains underexplored. Herein, we report the first vanadium(II) photosensitizer for PDT and show that its biological activity can be unlocked through loading into human serum albumin (HSA), a strategy intended to improve its pharmacological properties. The resulting HSA-bound complex showed negligible dark toxicity and induced pronounced light-dependent cytotoxicity upon blue- and red-light irradiation in human colon carcinoma cells. Mechanistic studies revealed that the HSAbound complex preferentially accumulates in lysosomes, where red-light irradiation triggers singlet oxygen generation and promotes apoptosis. This work establishes vanadium(II) complexes as a new class of photosensitizers for photodynamic therapy and opens new opportunities for the design of first-row transition-metal photosensitizers with improved photophysical properties.
items.authors: Zisis Papadopoulos, Aimée Marie Irgel, Alexandra König, Katja Heinze, Johannes Karges

items.title: Report – 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop
items.abstract: The Ontologies4Chem workshop series brings together developers and users of chemical ontologies to align ontology initiatives with shared standards and approaches to semantic interoperability. The 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop, organized by TIB in collaboration with the Beilstein-Institute, the NFDI4Chem Consortium, the NFDI4Cat Consortium, and the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) took place from November 11 to 13, 2025 in Limburg an der Lahn (Hessen, Germany). The programme covered chemical ontologies and their applications on the first day, the ontological representation of chemical reactions and experimental workflows on the second, and the reuse and further development of ChEBI as the central resource for chemical entities on the third. Talks on RO-Crate, DCAT-AP+, and chemDCAT-AP added the provenance and packaging layer that complements ontologies in FAIR data workflows. A central outcome of the workshop is the introduction of the Ontologies4Chem Canon, a vision of a living, community-curated body of the essential ontologies for chemistry together with their design patterns and the discourse around them. It rests on modular, OBO-aligned design, reuse before creation, the IUPAC Gold Book as source of definitions, and ODK-based development and deployment pipelines, provided by the NFDI4Chem Terminology Service and related internally through SSSOM mappings. The hacking sessions initiated the migration of the CHEMINF ontology to an ODK-based infrastructure and led to a decision, taken together with the ChEBI team, to reincorporate disjointness axioms into the ChEBI release cycle. Presentations on ontology pre-training, ChemLog, and Chebifier 2 showed how ontologies and machine learning reinforce each other. A panel discussion with the ChEBI team identified sustainable, community-driven governance and funding as the decisive challenges for the field.
items.authors: Oliver Koepler, Philip Strömert, Johannes Hunold, Sabrina Krohm, Noura Rayya, Samantha Pearman-Kanza

items.title: Multimodal LLM-Assisted Diagnosis of Cryptic Failure Modes in High-Throughput Experimentation: A Case Study in Gold Nanorod Synthesis
items.abstract: Self-driving labs typically optimize experiments within a predefined design space. Yet high-throughput campaigns can fail for reasons outside this design space, in-cluding reagent state, stock solution quality, and handling history. Here, we present a case study of a five-plate high-throughput gold nanorod synthesis campaign in which a multimodal large language model (LLM) helped diagnose such cryptic failure modes. We used low-cost camera images for rapid assessment of seed and synthesis state, with UV–vis spectroscopy when the images were insufficient for failure diagnosis. The campaign included an abnormal seed batch, a visually plausible synthesis with hidden spectroscopic defects, and a plate-wide failed synthesis in which most wells showed weak spectra with a strong rise toward the near-infrared. In response, the LLM intervened by questioning the seed preparation step and reagent handling instead of optimizing the screened concentrations of silver nitrate and ascorbic acid. To quantify recovery, we defined a UV–vis spectral roughness metric based on local spectral interpolation across the synthesis grid. The final synthesis had the lowest roughness, Rspec = 0.636 compared with ∼ 0.772 for earlier successful runs, and the highest median longitudinal-window absorbance. Our results show the potential of multimodal LLMs upstream of autonomous optimization in self-driving labs to identify when an experiment has failed for reasons outside the nominal design space and when additional characterization is needed before optimization should continue.
items.authors: Riya Patel, Gabriela Briceno, Amirali Aghazadeh, Vida Jamali

items.title: Synthesis of Dihydro-indolo-oxazines via a RedOx‑Neutral, Gold‑Catalyzed Hydride‑Transfer Process
items.abstract: RedOx neutral gold-mediated processes are particularly valuable for C-H bond functionalization. When these transformations proceed stepwise via intramolecular hydride transfer to an electrophilic Gold(I) center, their efficiency critically depends on the nature of the hydride donor. We report herein that, in contrast to tertiary amines, which strongly coordinate to gold and thereby tend to inhibit catalysis, benzyl ethers can serve as effective hydride donors, enabling a smooth catalytic C-H functionalization sequence. This reactivity is illustrated by the synthesis of a series of dihydro-indolo-oxazines, obtained in moderate to high yields under mild catalytic conditions.
items.authors: Elyssa Caron, Fabien Gagosz

items.title: Carbonylative Cross Couplings Promoted by a Metal Carbonyl Complex in Catalytic Amounts
items.abstract: Carbon monoxide is a highly valuable building block that enables the rapid construction of complex molecules like pharmaceuticals from simple and commercial precursors. However, the handling of CO requires special and elaborate precautions, since it is a highly toxic and odourless gas supplied in pressurized gas cylinders. To improve operations with carbon monoxide several CO surrogates including Mo(CO) 6 have been introduced, which form CO in enclosed gas reactors on demand. Herein, we report on the discovery of Fe 2 (CO) 9 as a highly efficient CO surrogate, which unlike preceding works is capable to transfer 8 out of 9 CO ligands onto the molecule of interest. This enables the application diiron nonacarbonyl in “catalytic amount” of 15 mol% with regard to the aryl halide coupling partner (100 mol%). The high synthetic value of the novel approach is witnessed by three different carbonylative cross couplings, syntheses of four pharmaceuticals and a head-to-head comparison with Mo(CO) 6 as gold standard.
items.authors: Djavid Mohammadi, Richard Tröltzsch, Jonas Surkau, Karsten Lüdtke, Peter H. Huy

items.title: Dielectric Nanolensing: How a Wavelength-Scale Lens Carries Hidden Detail into an Ordinary Microscope and What Chemistry Should Build Next
items.abstract: Dielectric nanolensing has evolved from a wavelength-scale molecular lens into a broad family of microsphere, particle-lens, scanning, arrayed, and computational platforms. Breakthrough advances now include white-light nanoscopy, immersed high-index imaging, large-field scanning, non-destructive semiconductor metrology, living-cell optics, nanolithography, and substrate-free Raman analysis. This Perspective explains, in accessible terms, how a lens placed in the specimen’s near field can redirect otherwise inaccessible spatial information into light collected by an ordinary objective. It then reconciles curvature, solid immersion, nanojets, Mie and whispering-gallery modes, and Fano interference as condition-dependent contributions rather than competing universal explanations. The central opportunity is forward-looking: chemistry can control complex refractive index, shape, assembly, environment, and the nanometre-scale lens-specimen gap, while quantitative transfer measurements can replace incomparable resolution claims. Together, these developments point toward scalable, calibrated nanolenses for imaging, metrology, and chemical analysis.
items.authors: Kwang S. Kim

items.title: Transitional Band Gaps During Polarization Switching in Wurtzite Ferroelectrics
items.abstract: The electronic band gap ( E g ) is commonly treated as a static materials property associated with an equilibrium crystal structure. Yet in functional materials whose operation involves field-driven structural transformations, the relevant electronic structure may evolve as the atoms traverse different configurations, with consequences for materials design and device reliability. Wurtzite ferroelectrics provide a compelling setting to examine this idea because polarization reversal requires substantial atomic rearrangement and unusually large electric fields that can approach dielectric breakdown. Here, using first-principles calculations, we track E g along atomistically resolved polarization switching minimum energy pathways in experimentally established Al 1−x Sc x N, Ga 1−x Sc x N, and Al 1−x B x N ferroelectric alloys. As cation-centered tetrahedra rearrange and invert during switching, the band gap decreases substantially relative to the equilibrium polar state, with reductions reaching approximately 30-40% in some compositions. Importantly, the minimum E g does not necessarily coincide with zero polarization or with the highest-energy configuration along the switching pathway, demonstrating that the energetic and electronic structure landscapes do not map trivially onto one another. Extending the analysis to 24 chemically diverse wurtzite compounds reveals transitional E g reductions ranging from negligible to nearly 50%. These results identify the minimum E g sampled along the switching trajectory as an important, material-specific descriptor of electronic robustness. The results also suggest an intrinsic contribution to transient excess conduction during switching and motivate future studies connecting transitional electronic structure to conductive domain walls and memristive behavior in ferroelectrics.
items.authors: Alice Brambati, Thi Nguyen, Cheng-Wei Lee, Bhawna Sahni, Geoff L. Brennecka, Prashun Gorai

items.title: Auto-healing Co(II)-based metallosupramolecular hydrogel of 3-amino-1-propanol as Low Molecular Weight Gelator: Investigations of morphological features, rheological dynamics, and stimuli-responsiveness
items.abstract: In the present work, a stable, green-coloured metallohydrogel was fabricated under ambient conditions through the spontaneous self-assembly of cobalt(II) nitrate hexahydrate, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, as the metal source with 3-amino-1-propanol acting as a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) in aqueous medium. The synthesized metallogel was characterized using rheological analysis i.e.; strain sweep, frequency sweep and thixotropy. Surface morphology and network texture were probed by FESEM, elemental composition was verified by EDX analysis, and the gel's stimuli-responsive were subsequently evaluated.
items.authors: Tripti Dolai, Prity Chatterjee, Mallika Sharma, Suresh Kumar Yatirajula, Amiya Dey

items.title: Evaluation of log D and pKa predictions for the SAMPL8 blind challenge
items.abstract: The goal of the Statistical Assessment of Modeling of Proteins and Ligands (SAMPL) challenge is to improve the accuracy of computational methods used in drug discovery and design by providing a platform to benchmark different methods and draw the community’s attention to specific areas of improvement. The SAMPL8 physical properties challenge focused on the prediction of pKa and log D for multi-protic compounds with two or more widely separated polar groups. Here, we present an overview of the results from the SAMPL8 challenge. We adopted two different workflows to compare experimental and predicted pKa data due to the presence of multiple macroscopic pKa values for individual compounds. These multiple pKa values meant that it was often unclear which of the microscopic transitions contributed to the observed macroscopic pKa. We find that the performance of different methods for pKa predictions is heavily dependent on how we pair predicted pKa values with measured ones–that is, the underlying mechanism. In contrast to some previous challenges, where analysis focused on pairing calculated pKa values with those which were experimentally closest, we here instead use alternate approaches, presenting two different methods of evaluating pKa predictions. Our first approach uses community consensus, pairing the most popular predicted transition(s) with the experimental value. The second involves selecting the correct transition based on additional experimental data–specifically, pH-dependent solubility curves. We used these two approaches to compare SAMPL submissions from participants using a wide variety of different methods. Results showed that while the numerical predictions for pKa values were often reasonable, different participating methods might disagree about the mechanism behind the pKa, indicating that pKa prediction methods may need to focus more on correct prediction of protonation states, not just pKa values. In the log D analysis we find that most methods performed better in prediction of log D for the octanol-water solvent combination, likely due to the greater abundance of training data for these solvents.
items.authors: Aakankschit Nandkeolyar, Nicolas Tielker, Stefan M. Kast, David L. Mobley

items.title: Linear I···I contacts in a platinum(IV)-diiodo porphyrin: Emergent type III halogen–halogen interactions
items.abstract: This study presents experimental and theoretical evidence for unusual intermolecular I···I interactions between axially coordinated iodide ligands in a Pt(IV) porphyrin. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that PtI2T[3,5-diOMe]PP, where T[3,5-diOMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, crystallises in the uncommon P4/n space group, in contrast to the I4/m space group frequently observed for related metalloporphyrins, and adopts an eclipsed columnar packing arrangement, with co-crystallised dichloromethane (DCM) molecules occupying the space between successive porphyrin layers. The iodide ligands form linear I···I contacts that propagate into a one-dimensional supramolecular network. Comparison with the axial-iodide-free PtT[3,5-diOMe]PP and the related OsI2T[2,4,6-triMe]PP, where T[2,4,6-triMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(2,4,6-trimethylphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, demonstrates how axial iodide coordination, peripheral substitution, and the local solvent environment influence the resulting crystal packing and macrocyclic conformation. Molecular surface electrostatic potential (MESP), quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM), natural bond orbital (NBO), and Hirshfeld surface analyses were employed to investigate the nature of the intermolecular contacts. QTAIM analysis identifies the I···I contacts as weak, closed-shell interactions, while NBO analysis reveals a significant donor–acceptor component involving iodide lone pairs and neighbouring Pt–I or Os–I antibonding orbitals. The magnitude and distribution of these interactions depend on the local supramolecular environment, with co-crystallised DCM contributing additional C–H···I contacts and altering the electronic environment of these ligands. Together, these results demonstrate that the I···I interactions cannot be considered in isolation, but instead form part of a broader network of cooperative intermolecular contacts that governs the crystal packing of the Pt(IV) porphyrin.
items.authors: Tristan K. Theunissen, Gerhard A. Venter, Catharine Esterhuysen, Abhik Ghosh, Susan A. Bourne

items.title: Addressing the nature and reductive stability of alkylthiol-modified Cu electrode surfaces
items.abstract: Cu surfaces modified with molecular adsorbates are being used in electrocatalyic processes (e.g., CO2 reduction (CO2RR)) to improve performance, but the nature and stability of molecular adsorbates (e.g. thiols) on Cu remain poorly understood owing to the sensitivity of Cu to oxidation and the complex chemical nature of the interface. To address these challenges, alkylthiol modification of 10 monolayers of electrodeposited Cu onto single-crystal Au bead electrodes has been prepared and studied using electrochemistry and in-situ fluorescence imaging. Under rigorous O2-free and H2O-free conditions, oxide-free Cu surfaces were produced. Modification of these oxide-free surfaces with alkylthiols resulted in a Cu2S overlayer. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiol in the presence of trace H2O or O2 was found to have an increased amount of Cu2S, identified by electrochemistry and ex-situ Raman. The reductive stability of the alkylthiol modified Cu surface was investigated using a fluorophore-labelled DNA-alkylthiol adsorbate and in-situ fluorescence microscopy. Oxide-free Cu surfaces modified with alkylthiols produced a surface that was slightly more reductively stable (by-0.1 to-0.2V) when compared with alkylthiol self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) on Au, but do not show the characteristics of an alkyl-thiol SAM. Under similar modification procedures but using slightly oxidized Cu surfaces, the adsorbates were not removed using reducing potentials more negative than hydrogen evolution, suggesting a multilayer adsorbate structure composed of Cu2S with non-specifically adsorbed species. Thus, Cu surfaces prepared in the presence of trace O2and H2O may have a Cu-sulfide overlayer rather than a Cu-alkylthiol monolayer, even at reducing potentials typical of CO2RR or other electrocatalysis processes. More generally, the quantitative methodology that we developed for studying Cu electrodes is a framework for gaining insight into the preparation and molecular modification of other non-noble metal electrodes of interest for electrocatalysis.
items.authors: Daina V. Baker, Gilberto Martinez-Blanco, W. Russ Algar, Dan Bizzotto

items.title: Cuban Bentonite/Polymer Nanocomposites: A Sustainable Alternative for Food Packaging
items.abstract: The environmental impact of conventional polymers has driven the search for sustainable food packaging alternatives. Clay incorporation into polymers matrices has shown to enhance optical, mechanical, and barrier properties. This study evaluates Cuban natural bentonite as a reinforcing phase in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), plus their mixtures (PVA/PVP and PVA/CMC). Films were cast and characterized by XRD, ATR-FTIR, SEM, and water resistance tests; opacity was measured by UV-Vis spectroscopy accounting for thickness. Results indicate that polymer dispersion depends on temperature (CMC fastest). Bent/HPMC films stood out for their superior opacity and water resistance, while Bent/PVA/PVP and Bent/PVA/CMC showed predominantly exfoliated structures, favorable for food packaging applications.
items.authors: C. Leal, D. Hernández, M. Muñoz-Arias, E. Altshuler, A. Rivera

items.title: Counter-Intuitive Orthogonal Catalysis for In-Situ Functionalization of High-Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
items.abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption.
